question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of intermittent palpitations that occur when he is stressed, exercising, or when he drinks alcohol. Physical examination shows an irregularly irregular pulse. An ECG shows irregular QRS complexes without any discrete P waves. Pharmacotherapy with carvedilol is initiated for his condition. Compared to treatment with propranolol, which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Carvedilol -> Non-selective beta-blocker -> Blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors -> Less likely to cause bronchospasm compared to propranolol -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Carvedilol -> Blocks beta-1 receptors -> Less likely to cause bradycardia compared to propranolol -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Carvedilol -> Blocks beta-1 receptors -> Less likely to cause hypotension compared to propranolol -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Carvedilol -> Blocks beta-2 receptors -> Less likely to cause hyperglycemia compared to propranolol -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Carvedilol -> Blocks beta-1 receptors -> Less likely to cause hyperkalemia compared to propranolol -> 95%
analysis: Carvedilol is a non-selective beta-blocker with alpha-blocking activity commonly used to manage atrial fibrillation. Compared to propranolol, carvedilol is less likely to cause bradycardia due to its additional alpha-blocking properties.
